title: L6 · Membranes & Skin
subtitle: Body membranes, skin functions, layers, glands, hair, nails

lines.text: There are four body membranes.
Three are epithelial. One is connective tissue.
The **cutaneous** membrane is the skin. It is the only dry membrane.
**Serous** membranes line cavities closed to the outside.
**Mucous** membranes line cavities open to the outside.
**Synovial** membranes line joints. They have no epithelium.
Serous membranes are always double.
The **parietal** layer lines the body wall.
The **visceral** layer covers the organ.
Serous fluid between them reduces friction.
**Pleurae** wrap the lungs. **Pericardium** wraps the heart. **Peritoneum** lines the abdomen.
Mucous membranes line the respiratory, digestive and urogenital tracts.
Their epithelium sits on loose tissue called the **lamina propria**.
**Mucus** lubricates and traps.
Synovial membranes line joints, bursae and tendon sheaths.
They make **synovial fluid**, a very good lubricant.
Skin is the largest organ.
**Keratin** protects against damage and drying out.
The **acid mantle** and white blood cells protect against germs.
**Melanin** protects against UV.
The nervous system controls skin temperature.
To lose heat, sweat evaporates and vessels dilate. That's **vasodilation**.
To keep heat, vessels constrict and goosebumps rise. That's **vasoconstriction**.
It is **negative feedback**, just like Lecture 1.
**Meissner's** corpuscles sense light touch and two-point discrimination.
**Merkel** discs sense light touch, edges and points.
**Pacinian** corpuscles sense deep pressure. The Pacific Ocean is deep.
Nociceptors sense pain.
**Ruffini** senses heat. It sounds Italian, and Italy is hot.
**Krause** senses cold. It sounds like Santa Claus, and winter is cold.
Sweat excretes urea, ammonia, salt and water.
Skin makes **vitamin D**, melanin, keratin and immune proteins.
It stores **carotene**, a yellow-orange antioxidant.
Don't confuse carotene with keratin.
Skin color comes from melanin, carotene and hemoglobin. Low oxygen looks blue. That's cyanosis.
The **epidermis** is on top. It is keratinized stratified squamous, and avascular.
The **dermis** is below. It is connective tissue, and vascular.
The **hypodermis** is fat below the dermis.
It is not a layer of skin.
Top to bottom: Come Let's Get Sun Burned.
Stratum **corneum** is thickest. Its cells are dead.
Stratum **lucidum** is only in thick skin, on palms and soles.
Stratum **granulosum** is grainy. Cells start to die and fill with keratin.
Stratum **spinosum** is spiny. It holds Langerhans cells.
Stratum **basale** is deepest. Cells divide here, and melanocytes live here.
The **papillary** layer is the top fifth. It is areolar tissue.
Its **dermal papillae** make fingerprints and hold Meissner's corpuscles.
The **reticular** layer is the deep four fifths. It is dense irregular tissue.
It holds hair follicles, glands and Pacinian corpuscles.
All skin glands are exocrine. They have ducts.
**Sebaceous** glands make oil, called sebum. They empty into hair follicles.
**Eccrine** sweat glands are small and everywhere. They open at pores and cool the body.
**Apocrine** glands are large, in the armpits and groin. They start at puberty.
**Ceruminous** glands make earwax.
A hair has a **root** in the follicle and a **shaft** you can see.
The papilla brings it blood.
The **arrector pili** is a smooth muscle. It makes goosebumps.
Nails are mostly keratin. The **lunula** is the moon near the cuticle.
The **rule of nines** splits the body into areas of 9 percent each.
A first degree burn is the epidermis only, like sunburn.
Second degree reaches the dermis. It blisters.
Third degree is full thickness. It looks white or black.
Fourth degree reaches muscle and bone.
